note: Normative. Both a sender's shim and a receiver read this file, and each has a conformance test against it, so a vocabulary that drifts on one side is a test failure rather than a discovery. Every list is CLOSED: a value outside it is rejected, not accepted with a warning.

parts.note: What surrounds the model. A part nobody named is a part that can change without the identity changing, which is the defect this vocabulary exists to close.

model_parts.note: What answered, as opposed to what surrounded it. Closed for the same reason parts are: a model part nobody named is one that can change while every name stays the same. Each value is here because the distillation record shows answers moving while it changed and the names did not.

rationale.checkpoint: Every file the process read from the model artifact: parameters, adapters, tokenizer, chat template, configuration. A retrain with the same script and seed agreed with its predecessor on 93.4% of labels under the same model name. Digest: for each file, sorted by the utf-8 bytes of its POSIX path relative to the artifact root, append '<path>\t<sha256 of the file>\n', where the path is the path within the artifact, not the target of a symlink, and the sha256 is the lowercase hex of the bytes the path resolves to; a path containing a tab or a newline makes the part extraction_failed. Re-serialising identical tensors changes this digest, which is the safe direction.
rationale.precision: The numeric transform in force once loading finished, read off the loaded parameters rather than the configuration: one 'dtype.<name>=<parameter count>' line per dtype, 'quantisation=<scheme or none>', 'device=<type>', sorted, '\n'-terminated. Dynamic int8 quantisation at load left the stored bytes unchanged and agreed with the GPU on 33-40% of labels. A value the collector could not resolve (a dtype of 'auto') is extraction_failed, not a guess.
rationale.runtime: The code that computes the answer: one '<distribution>==<version>' line per package the collector declares it reads, resolved in the answering process at load, sorted, '\n'-terminated. The package list is part of the collector, static per collector version. A rebuilt serving image lost packages and the teacher re-answered 97 of 100 the same. An image or lockfile digest may be a label; it changes on every rebuild and is not what computed the answer.
rationale.answer_mode: Where the answer is taken from, one value of answer_modes, digested as its utf-8 bytes. A student trained to compare three label scores generated '1111' when asked to generate.

answer_modes.note: Where an answer comes from. Closed and descriptive: it says what produced the answer, never which is better.

rationale.generated_text: Text sampled from the language-model head, read out by the caller.
rationale.option_scores: Scores from the language-model head over a declared option set, the best option taken.
rationale.classifier_output: Scores from a head that is not a language-model head, such as a gradient-boosted classifier over features (for example a LightGBM student).

lineage.note: How a tuned model came to be: a document its trainer writes, outside any record, about one artifact. Never identifying -- two trainings that produced the same bytes are the same model -- and pushed by nature, because whoever serves the result holds the bytes and not their history. A lineage claim may trigger a refusal and may never lift one; an absent lineage, a missing ancestor or a set digest with no manifest is unknown, never clean.

rationale.subject: The artifact_identity this document is about. A lineage whose subject differs from the artifact observed is read as absent: the history of an earlier training beside the bytes of a later one would otherwise describe a model that is not there.
rationale.parent: The parent's artifact_identity, or 'none'. A quantised or merged child lists no sets of its own, so a receiver that checks training overlap walks the chain; a missing ancestor is unknown.
rationale.sets: Item sets by the sha256 of their manifest file. 'excluded' is not a role: by the subtract-only rule it could have no effect.
rationale.signal: What the training signal came from (a teacher, a grader, a reward): an artifact_identity, a content digest, or a label. A label is unverifiable and never matches anything.

sourcing.note: How a fact reached the receiver. These are not interchangeable: they differ in what the fact can support.

rationale.in_the_request: The bytes are held. It IS what was sent: verifiable and contemporaneous.
rationale.loaded_by_us: The collector runs in the process that loaded the model and digested what it loaded, during this load. The only sourcing that can key a model identity: a request never carries weights, and a certificate was once issued over bytes that no longer existed under an unchanged name. A digest cached from an earlier load is pulled_by_us with a lag equal to its age; a stamp relayed verbatim by a router or gateway keeps this sourcing, and a stamp read back over a separate request is pulled_by_us.
rationale.pulled_by_us: Fetched, so verifiable and NOT contemporaneous. Carries its lag; a lag nobody bounded cannot support a per-request claim.
rationale.pushed_by_owner: A declaration. Not checkable by the receiver, and a label the owner controls can stay fixed while the thing under it changes.
rationale.not_observable: No mode reaches it. A tool's implementation behind an unchanged schema is the case that forced this entry.

boundaries.note: What a digest is a digest OF. Three things were being called 'the bytes', and the two mistakes they cause run in opposite directions, so neither is fixed by being careful.

rationale.transport: What a client put on the wire. Two client versions serialise differently and decode to the same text, so keying on this SPLITS runs that were identical.
rationale.parsed: The protocol value after decoding. Two strings that canonicalise to one value can behave differently embedded verbatim in a prompt, so keying on this MERGES runs that were not.
rationale.model_visible: The text the requester supplied for the model to read, before any chat template the server applies and before any prompt a provider adds (SPEC section 2). The only boundary that can support a claim that two runs had the same input. A request_template digest is at this boundary although the requester decides where its holes are: that can split identical input, the safe direction (SPEC section 2.1).

never_identifying.note: Parts that may never key an identity whatever their sourcing and boundary say. Enforced by name because the general rules would admit them.

rationale.tool_trace: Bytes we hold, so the sourcing rule admits it -- and it is a per-run OUTCOME, unique per run, so keying on it makes every pair of runs incomparable.

refines_only.note: Parts that may refine an identity another identifying part establishes and may never establish one. A record whose only identifying parts are in this list has no harness identity. Needed because what such a part names is decided by a requester's declaration nobody can check (SPEC section 1.1a): it may split two runs a held instruction would otherwise join, and must never give an identity to a run that has none.

rationale.request_template: The template names the fixed text of the non-system messages, and which text is fixed and which fills a hole is the requester's split. Beside another identifying part it can only split: two runs under one system message whose user-message wrappers differ get two identities instead of one. On its own it would join runs on the requester's word: two runs declaring the same fixed text, one of which appended a block to the text in a hole, would share an identity that version 2 gave neither. The case it separates is unmeasured; the part is motivated by R17a, where the same instruction in the user message instead of nowhere moved accuracy 4.58 points and an irrelevant suffix of about 150 tokens in the user message moved it 0.898 to 0.858, both without a system message and so without an identity in either version.

must_be_known_for_identity.note: Parts whose state a record must know to have a harness identity: each must be held, in any sourcing, or absent with the reason in known_when_absent_as. A record in which one of these is absent for any other reason, or is not mentioned, has no harness identity: the collector could not show that the part was not there, and an identity computed without it would join runs that differ in it. The list names the parts that some binding makes model_visible and in_the_request; a binding that makes another part so needs this list amended, which is a change of version. A collector that cannot reach request_template therefore gives no record a harness identity unless it can see that the request carries no template.

absence_reasons.note: Why a part is not in the record, and WHOSE absence it is. A single undifferentiated hole cannot serve, because a collector that loses the ability to read a part writes the same absence a sender's silence writes -- and then every consumer behaves exactly as designed while the regression is invisible. A closed vocabulary constrains spelling, not truth.

white_space.note: The code points SPEC section 1.2 calls white space, the Unicode White_Space property, for the emptiness tests of section 1.2 and section 9 and nothing else: U+0009-U+000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000. U+001F and U+FEFF are not white space here, whatever a language's trim does.

status.note: Whether a record is complete about ITSELF. Separate from anything about the sender, because the two refusals are about different objects: toward the sender a collector is maximally permissive, and about itself it must be exact.

context_crossings.note: What crosses between two contexts, which is what decides whether splitting them is cheap. Counting contexts is not enough: the three have opposite economics.

rationale.briefs_and_results: Both caches stay warm, because neither context ever switches model. This is the arrangement a published 39.2% saving rests on.
rationale.whole_history: The transcript is copied, so the entire prefix is billed as fresh input in the second context. The split COSTS rather than saves, and it is indistinguishable from the row above in any record that only counts contexts.

tool_determinism.note: What a tool's contract promises for the same effective invocation context. Not a boolean: the third value, nobody said, is the common one and must not collapse into either of the others.
tool_determinism.rationale: A divergence between two traces on the same occasion is evidence of divergent recorded execution and never proof of a different tool implementation. Firing on argument equality alone was refuted three ways: it fires against a single run that writes a key and then reads it, it fires on essentially every networked tool because request ids sit in response bodies, and its conclusion is false even where firing is right.

occasion.note: What must match before two tool calls are the same occasion. Anything else is a different occasion and says nothing about the tool. The prefix is what stops the rule firing against a single run.

billed_legs.note: The legs a price card actually bills, which is four and not two. The cache discount attaches to the SHAPE of a request rather than to its text: identical content measured a 0% cache rate as one long message and 99.9% as a growing conversation.

attributes.note: The wire form. Flat, scalar-valued, and prefixed, so it rides on a span any tracer already emits. Indexed keys use the part name rather than an integer, because an integer index reorders and a part name does not.

record.perigraph.spec_version: integer. The format, so a reader can tell what it is looking at.
record.perigraph.collector: string. Which collector produced this record.
record.perigraph.collector_version: string. Its version. A part that stopped being readable between two versions cannot be attributed without it.
record.perigraph.collector_reaches: comma-separated part names. What this collector CLAIMS it can reach here, static per version -- a manifest that adapted to what it found could never contradict a record, which is the one thing it is for.
record.perigraph.model_reaches: comma-separated model part names. The model half's manifest: what this collector claims it can reach of checkpoint, precision, runtime and answer_mode, static per version, read and contradicted exactly as collector_reaches is.
record.perigraph.harness_identity: string or absent. Version 1's 'perigraph.identity', renamed in version 2. Over the identifying parts as section 2.2 serialises them, after the rules of refines_only and read_for_identity; for a record with no request_template part held, the same value version 2 gave.
record.perigraph.model_identity: string or absent. Over all four model parts, each loaded_by_us with a digest, sorted by part name, serialised as the harness identity is. Comparable only against another from the same collector and collector version, because precision and runtime are collector renderings. Stamped on every answer by the process that loaded the model.
record.perigraph.artifact_identity: string or absent. Over the checkpoint part alone, when it is loaded_by_us. Comparable across collectors: what a trainer can compute at save time and a lineage document can name.

per_part.perigraph.part.<name>.boundary: one of boundaries.values. Absent when there is no digest.
per_part.perigraph.part.<name>.digest: lowercase hex sha256 of the part's bytes at the stated boundary.
per_part.perigraph.part.<name>.label: optional, for a reader. Explicitly NOT a key: a version string the owner controls can stay fixed while the text under it changes. Never compared and never part of a digest or identity; a receiver may ignore it without dropping an absence.
per_part.perigraph.part.<name>.read_lag_seconds: number. Required for pulled_by_us and refused elsewhere.
per_part.perigraph.absent.<name>.detail: string. Required when the reason blames the collector, refused otherwise.

per_model_part.perigraph.model.<name>.digest: lowercase hex sha256 of the part's content as model_parts.rationale defines it. Model parts carry no boundary.
per_model_part.perigraph.model.<name>.label: optional, for a reader; never a key. A model name, a provider id, an image digest.
per_model_part.perigraph.model.<name>.read_lag_seconds: number. Required for pulled_by_us and refused elsewhere.
per_model_part.perigraph.model_absent.<name>.detail: string. Required when the reason blames the collector, refused otherwise.

extensions.perigraph.ext.<vendor>.<key>: reserved for attributes outside this specification. Never keys an identity, never lifts a refusal, and a receiver MUST NOT reject a record for carrying one (SPEC section 13.2).

receiver_obligations.note: What a receiver must do to claim conformance. Stated as refusals, because every one of them exists because a published number needed withdrawing.
must_refuse: A verdict over a record whose status is not complete.
A verdict over a record with no harness identity.
A verdict over a record where the collector's manifest claims a part the record reports not_reachable, or says nothing about.
An identity built on any digest whose boundary is not model_visible.
A comparison of two arms whose decisions were missing different facts, or where one recorded its missingness and the other did not.
A comparison of two conversations of different turn counts.
A statement of what an alternative would have cost when either side's context_partitioning is unrecorded.
A comparison where two traces diverge on the same occasion and the tool declared determinism.
A comparison of two `parsed` digests produced by different collectors or different collector versions.
A model identity or an artifact identity built on any part whose sourcing is not loaded_by_us.
A verdict over records grouped as one arm when the distinct harness identities derived from them number more than one, or number one while some record has none.
A verdict over records grouped as one arm that carry more than one model identity, or some with one and some without.
A claim bound to a model identity, applied to records that do not carry that model identity.
A comparison of two model identities produced by different collectors or different collector versions.
must_not_refuse: A record missing any number of parts. Toward the sender the collector is maximally permissive, and a collector that refuses a partial record produces no record at all.
A record whose status is not complete, as a LOG. It stays fully usable there.
A record with no model identity. A model served behind a provider's API stays admissible; claims about it are not bound to model bytes, and saying so is the receiver's job.
A record with no model half. Its model parts are read as unknown, not as not_observable: a hole nobody named, which a receiver reports rather than refuses, as it does any missing part.

digest.note: How a digest and an identity are computed. Stated exactly because SPEC section 6 alone does not say what bytes a string has, how the identity combines its parts, or that the result is truncated: a UTF-16 implementation would otherwise produce a different identity for every non-ASCII instruction while passing every test it wrote for itself.
digest.identity_serialisation: For each identifying part, sorted by part name ascending, append the bytes of '<part_name>=<content_digest>;' in utf-8. Digest the concatenation and take the first identity_length characters of the lowercase hex.
digest.model_visible_payload: Hashed RAW. No canonicalisation, no trimming, no case folding. A model reads the string and not its meaning. A request_template digest is over model-visible strings with the framing of request_template_serialisation: it may split runs whose model input was identical, because the requester places the holes, and it never joins two runs whose fixed strings differ, except that two templates fixing only white space are both treated as not sent.
digest.parsed_digests_are_collector_local: A `parsed` digest is comparable ONLY against another digest from the same collector and the same collector version. The two reference implementations serialise protocol values differently -- Python's repr renders 0.0 as '0.0' and JSON.stringify renders it as '0' -- so the same request yields different `parsed` digests in each. This is stated rather than fixed because a `parsed` digest can never key an identity, so nothing that matters was lost; what was at risk before saying it is somebody comparing two and concluding the harnesses differed.
digest.instruction_join: Where several system messages are present, join their contents with a single U+000A in the order they appear. This is NORMATIVE rather than collector-local, because the instruction digest keys the identity and two collectors choosing differently would give two identities for one request.
digest.model_identity_serialisation: As identity_serialisation, over the four model parts: '<part_name>=<content_digest>;' for each, sorted by part name, utf-8, sha256, first identity_length hex characters. artifact_identity is the same over the checkpoint part alone.
digest.request_template_serialisation: Over the request_template entries, one per message in order: the utf-8 bytes of '<m>:', where m is the number of entries; then for each entry '<r>:<role><k>:', where r is the utf-8 byte length of the role and k the number of fixed strings (0 for an untemplated entry); then for each fixed string '<n>:<string>', where n is its utf-8 byte length. Every number is decimal ASCII with no sign and no leading zeros. Every fixed string is included, empty ones too, so a string fixed before the hole and the same string fixed after it digest differently. The fixed strings are model-visible text and are not canonicalised. The entry count and the roles are digested as well, so the digest also changes with the number and the roles of the messages, untemplated ones included; the framing is injective.
